title: Workspace Heartbeat MCP Plugin v1
goal: Provide reliable operator-visible progress for each substantial ChatGPT assistant response through one atomic turn-begin operation, explicit turn-scoped updates, semantic-delta-first cadence, and one self-refreshing card that preserves the full bounded current-turn semantic history while retaining task-level history separately.
acceptance_criteria: Expose heartbeat_begin_turn(task_id, message, state) as the first Heartbeat operation for every substantial assistant response.

heartbeat_begin_turn atomically supersedes the prior active turn for the same conversation/task, generates an opaque server-owned turn_id, records the first heartbeat, and mounts the current-turn card.
Require explicit task_id + turn_id on every later heartbeat_update and reject missing, unknown, wrong-task, superseded, completed, or cross-conversation turn IDs without writing history.
Use openai/session only for conversation ownership checks, never as the primary turn-routing key.
Allow exactly one active heartbeat writer per durable task; reject a different conversation while ownership remains active.
Release in-memory task ownership when a terminal done heartbeat closes the turn.

Keep heartbeat_snapshot app-only/read-only and strictly scoped to task_id + turn_id with bounded full turn_history, latest-three recent compatibility projection, and active/superseded/completed state.
Make superseded/completed old cards stop polling and remain static historical transcript UI.
Keep heartbeat_get as explicit task-level history/sidebar inspection across turns.
Keep per-task sequence numbers monotonic while the server process is alive and retain bounded in-memory history.
Require Node.js 20 or newer and gate deployment with node --check server.js plus the complete plugin test suite.
Use a cache-busted live resource URI for v0.4.5.
Fail closed for stale conversations using old tool schemas; after Heartbeat tool/schema/UI changes, refresh the plugin and start a new conversation.
Preserve semantic-delta-first progress prose with exactly one heartbeat_begin_turn per assistant response and a 10-non-heartbeat-tool anti-silence backstop.

Live acceptance must prove a current turn with at least five semantic updates remains readable in one bounded scrollable card, then a second assistant response supersedes/freezes the prior card and starts an isolated new turn.
Keep the accepted v0.4.4 runtime as production rollback until v0.4.5 live acceptance passes.
The full current-turn card auto-follows new updates only when the operator is already near the bottom; deliberate upward scrolling is preserved across refreshes.
Preserve recent as a latest-three compatibility projection while adding bounded turn_history; do not mix prior assistant turns into the current card.
constraints: Use current documented OpenAI/MCP Apps APIs and a ChatGPT thread entrypoint; do not depend on hidden client behavior.
Do not expose private chain-of-thought; heartbeat_update carries concise operator-facing progress prose only.
Do not commit per-heartbeat runtime state to Git.
Do not add OAuth, a database, cloud hosting, durable history, or SSE/event streaming until the stable polling/history loop is proven.

Do not claim this MCP server can physically block unrelated GitHub or other external tool calls; the 10-tool anti-silence backstop remains an executor contract unless operations are later proxied through a controllable orchestrator.
Do not automatically reset the panel to IDLE on assistant-response start because the current MCP App surface does not provide a reliable response-start lifecycle event.
Keep all implementation inside workspace-control plugins/workspace-heartbeat/** plus this task capsule/handoff.
Do not depend on undocumented control of inline MCP App placement; ChatGPT owns inline surface ordering, so chronology-sensitive routine updates must not attach custom inline UI.
Do not rely on native assistant commentary as the guaranteed heartbeat delivery path; long-turn stress testing showed intermediate commentary can be truncated after early tool operations.
Do not attach UI to heartbeat_update itself; otherwise one card per update can be host-collected at the bottom.
Do not assert that MCP Apps host guarantees immediate initial iframe mount; accept only observed live user UI evidence.
Use app-only visibility for heartbeat_snapshot and require an explicit task_id so one live view cannot conflate task histories.
Do not ask the model to poll heartbeat_snapshot; the live iframe owns the refresh loop.
heartbeat_render is retired; do not reintroduce repeated model-side render snapshots as the routine progress path.
Do not ask the model to call heartbeat_snapshot; the mounted app owns the live refresh loop.
Do not claim a new heartbeat runtime accepted merely because source tests pass; changing the runtime target requires live host validation.

notes:
The user explicitly wants heartbeat delivery to be a tool call and the UI to be one updating formatted box, while heartbeat prose remains natural and conversational. Live evidence now proves the thread side panel renders in normal Chat mode. The first authorization attempt using 'Use once' produced an 'Unable to load conversation' error; retrying after refresh with 'Always allow' allowed the chat to continue. The research chat claimed the live heartbeat panel was working before the user had observed any panel; such model prose is not accepted as evidence. The MCP server currently logs startup/errors only, not successful requests, so an idle MCP terminal cannot prove that no request occurred. System Node v12.22.9 is unsupported for this implementation; Node 20 in a dedicated conda environment is the working runtime. tmux helpers heartbeat-up/heartbeat-status/heartbeat-console/heartbeat-down keep both MCP and ngrok alive across SSH disconnects. New live evidence proved transport and rendering but exposed a session-correlation defect: the panel sometimes polled heartbeat_get under a different or missing ChatGPT session identity, received no task, switched to IDLE, and later resurrected the prior heartbeat. The v0.2 correction makes task_id authoritative, retains bounded task history, persists active task/history in widget state, ignores empty polls after valid state, declares Node >=20, and logs successful MCP requests. The user's preferred UX is a sequential heartbeat log that does not disappear between updates. Automatic reset to IDLE on assistant-response start is intentionally deferred because no reliable response-start lifecycle signal is available. The panel-stability correction is repository-valid and canonical at 3214ec2be4f0c20933784b3d265386d9652dfd0b. The task is now blocked only on the user's live Lambda/ChatGPT smoke. Fresh-chat v0.2 field evidence on 2026-10-05: the first heartbeat rendered as WORKING with a footer showing 1 retained update and remained visible throughout an approximately 1m56s response. The prior false-IDLE/disappearing behavior was not observed. No second heartbeat was emitted during that run, so multi-heartbeat sequential accumulation remains the sole pending live acceptance check. Do not repeat the single-heartbeat smoke; use normal research work to obtain the next qualifying multi-update observation. Additional field evidence: after earlier v0.2 heartbeats landed, a later heartbeat_update returned UNAVAILABLE. This makes end-to-end delivery availability a separate open failure from the already-corrected false-IDLE UI bug. Do not infer the cause without correlating the model-visible UNAVAILABLE with MCP server and ngrok request evidence. New field evidence: with the v0.2 panel open, successful POST /mcp requests streamed roughly once per second. This is directly explained by setInterval(refresh, 1000) in heartbeat-panel.html. OpenAI's current MCP Apps documentation recommends receiving model tool results through ui/notifications/tool-result; the one-second window.openai.callTool polling loop is therefore unnecessary as the primary update mechanism and may contribute to intermittent UNAVAILABLE failures. The v0.3 correction is implemented at f542f3bed7a3555877eb7bff14a38b13a4921692: it uses the MCP Apps ui/notifications/tool-result lifecycle as the primary UI update path, retains a 5s/15s/30s adaptive reconciliation fallback, skips active reconciliation while hidden, bumps the resource URI to panel-v3.html, and adds a static panel contract test. Repository and live validation are pending. Additional live evidence: the v0.3 mounted panel successfully retained two sequential updates at once, proving multi-heartbeat chronological accumulation. However, the five-second reconciliation fallback still generated recurring 400/200/202 MCP request clusters. The design was therefore simplified again to v0.3.1: event-driven ui/notifications/tool-result only, no automatic tools/call, no reconciliation timer, no background heartbeat_get polling, with panel-v4.html as a fresh resource key.
